business_problem: An operator drilling deeper and more complex horizontal wells in Colombia needed to reduce trajectory uncertainty, drilling risk, and well-quality issues caused by complex geology, subsurface seismic faults, collision avoidance constraints, casing-setting depth limits, torque and drag, and other well design constraints.
solution_summary: Halliburton implemented an autonomous drilling workflow for three horizontal wells in Colombia that combined LOGIX™ drilling performance with LOGIX™ automation and remote operations and the iCruise® intelligent rotary steerable system. Downhole intelligent sensors embedded in the iCruise RSS supplied operational data from the wellbore, which was integrated into continuous predictive models. LOGIX drilling performance used machine learning together with a digital twin and a physics-based bottomhole assembly model to move the operator from descriptive optimization to predictive analytics for real-time trajectory design. LOGIX automation and remote operations connected these models with the remote drilling center, multiple PSLs, and the directional engineer so recommendations could be applied during well construction. The source does not name a separate storage product, but it describes continuous model access to live drilling data to predict future conditions, reduce uncertainty, and keep execution aligned with planned DDI and KPI targets.

solution_components.name: LOGIX™ drilling performance
solution_components.role: Runs the predictive analytics workflow, combining machine learning with physics-based models to optimize well trajectories and predict future drilling conditions.

solution_components.name: LOGIX™ automation and remote operations
solution_components.role: Coordinates automation, remote operations, and model-driven recommendations across the drilling team and remote center during well construction.

solution_components.name: iCruise® intelligent rotary steerable system
solution_components.role: Provides intelligent sensing and steerable drilling capability that feeds real-time downhole data into the predictive drilling workflow.

data_flow: Downhole intelligent sensors in the iCruise® intelligent rotary steerable system capture live drilling data, which feeds LOGIX™ drilling performance models that combine machine learning, a digital twin, and a physics-based BHA model. Predictions and trajectory recommendations are then delivered through LOGIX™ automation and remote operations to the remote drilling center and directional engineer for execution during well construction.
business_outcome: The operator improved drilling consistency and trajectory accuracy across three horizontal wells, increasing rate of penetration, improving casing and liner running speed, reducing tortuosity, and lowering time and effort needed to keep wells on the planned path.
metrics: 15 to 45% improvement in casing and liner running speed
architecture_clues: Applied in three horizontal wells in the western Llanos basin in Colombia.
The platform analyzes extensive downhole data integrated with a digital twin and a physics-based model of the BHA.
The deployment integrated multiple PSLs with a remote drilling center.
The workflow was designed to maintain close alignment between planned and actual directional difficulty index (DDI).
